top.title: Red Sox have ‘massive human,’ former first-round pick as roster candidates
top.description: LAS VEGAS — The Rule 5 Draft didn’t take place during the 2021-22 offseason, the last time Major League Baseball owners locked out players. This offseason’s Rule 5 Draft again is in jeopardy with a lockout expected to begin at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. “We’re operating as though that would go on as normal,” Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow said at the GM Meetings. Teams have until Nov. 17 to add eligible players to their 40-man roster to protect them from being available to other teams in the draft. The Red Sox have several borderline candidates to be protected in Mikey Romero , Blake Wehunt , Brooks Brannon , Hayden Mullins , Johanfran Garcia , Braiden Ward , Angel Bastardo and Yordanny Monegro. Baseball America ranks Bastardo, who Boston re-signed to a minor league contract at the start of the offseason, the highest-ranked prospect of the group. It lists Bastardo No. 15 organizationally, Romero No. 18 and Wehunt No. 19. SoxProspects.com ranks Wehunt No. 13, Bastardo 18th and Romero 22nd. The Sox don’t have any obvious no-doubt-about-it additions. So although Breslow said Boston will operate as if the draft will happen, perhaps the Sox will take their chances and add nobody to the 40-man roster with roster spots limited anways this offseason. That said, Romero, Wehunt and Bastardo are all interesting names to watch at the deadline next Tuesday. Romero might be the most intriguing Rule 5 Draft eligible player of the group because of his background as a first-round draft pick. The Red Sox selected him 24th overall in 2022, he’s still young and injuries have limited his development time in the minors. There’s still plenty of room to improve with more reps. Meanwhile, the Red Sox have a shortage in starting pitching depth, making Wehunt and Bastardo potential additions. Bastardo pitched out of the bullpen for the WooSox in 2026 in his return from Tommy John surgery but had previously been a starter throughout his minor league career. Romero, who turns 23 in January, posted disappointing overall statistics in 113 games for Triple-A Worcester in 2026. He batted .239 with a .305 on-base percentage, .375 slugging percentage, .680 OPS and 30 extra-base hits in 490 plate appearances. The left-handed hitter’s OPS was 112 points higher against righties than lefties. But some of the advanced metrics told a more positive story. Romero had the second highest hard-hit percentage (41.7%) among Worcester players (minimum 120 plate appearances) behind only Mickey Gasper , who had a 46.5% hard-hit percentage in 238 plate appearances. He also trailed only Gasper in average exit velocity (90.8 mph) and adjusted exit velocity (92.5 mph) for WooSox hitters with 120 or more plate appearances. Additionally, he cut down on his strikeout percentage considerably, going from 30.2% with Worcester in 2025 to 21.0% in 2026. He closed out the year fairly strong, batting .270 with a .350 on-base percentage, .421 slugging percentage and .771 OPS in 143 plate appearances

top.title: What should the Oregon Ducks expect from Michigan's defense?
top.description: The Oregon Ducks will host the Michigan Wolverines at Autzen Stadium this weekend for the first time since 2003, but this time it will be the Wolverines looking to play spoiler to the Ducks ' postseason hopes. Michigan has the defense to do it, while the offense remains another story . With NFL talent and plenty of veteran leadership on hand, the moment in front of a raucous Oregon crowd shouldn't be too threatening to the Wolverines, and it could create a low-scoring affair. Oregon is fresh off a 41-28 blowout on the road over Ohio State , while Michigan fell at home to rival Michigan State, 15-6, despite keeping the Spartans out of the end zone. Michigan's defense has been up to the task against everyone on the schedule this season, but Oregon presents the biggest test yet. Conversely, the Ducks have been rolling on offense after making changes to the coaching staff, but the Wolverines might be a difficult matchup. The Ducks don't have any margin for error, but the Wolverines have a stout secondary and an aggressive front seven that could slow Oregon's momentum. Let's take a look at what Michigan does on defense schematically, who to watch out for, and what the Ducks might be able to do to put points on the board. What does Michigan do well on defense? Defensive coordinator Jay Hill operates out of an aggressive 4-2-5 nickel defense that relies on simulated pressures and physical play in the secondary. The Wolverines play more man coverage than the average defense, relying on defensive backs getting their hands on receivers to force them off their lines and tip passes away before an elite wideout has a chance. Michigan has limited opponents to 154.8 passing yards per game, fifth-best in the country. When playing zone coverage, Michigan runs plenty of different pressures while having an experienced front four that can get after the quarterback by itself. The Wolverines play out of the nickel to allow an extra rusher in different looks, and when a team comes out in 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends), the defense often shifts into a 4-3 look to help stop the run. That balance has helped Michigan rank among the best defenses in the country, limiting opponents to just 16.2 points per game (16th in the nation) and 100.6 rushing yards per game (17th). Players to Know DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley was the biggest transfer portal acquisition in the offseason for Michigan, following Kyle Whittingham from Utah, where he was a first-team All-American last season. Daley has picked up where he left off, leading the Wolverines with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. Michigan has several good pass rushers up front, including Dom Nichols and Tariq Boney, but Daley is by far the biggest threat that the Ducks will need to keep an eye on. He had his best game of the season last week against Michigan State, racking up eight tackles, two sacks and a forced fumble. The most humorous moment came not with Boras’ puns, but when his cell phone rang while speaking. He looked at his cell phone, moved the ringer to silent, and said, “Just another owner begging to meet with Skubal." The Los Angeles Dodgers , New York Mets , San Diego Padres and Toronto Blue Jays already have confirmed appointments. top.title: Lewis Hamilton demands Israel allows aid into Gaza after Rafah visit: ‘No excuse’
top.description: Lewis Hamilton has said Israel must let aid trucks into Gaza in a passionate Instagram post, a day after he toured the Rafah border crossing in Egypt . The seven-time Formula One world champion arrived in El Arish on Tuesday, and during the trip he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses. Following the visit, Hamilton took to Instagram to send a clear message to Israel and his 44.4 million followers. "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling. It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less," the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram. Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide and says its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants. Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go at the border that were regularly held up or faced major delays. Hamilton poses for a photo with Egyptian Red Crescent members (AFP/Getty) He said that at a nearby logistics centre, items had been rejected for "crazy reasons", including sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, and footballs for children. "Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse," he said. "I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away." Hamilton, 41, is an advocate for humanitarian causes. In 2021 he founded Mission 44, a charity that supports young people and works to improve their access to education and employment. The Brit is currently fourth in the F1 drivers’ standings, but is just a point behind third-placed George Russell, while he is only 18 adrift of Max Verstappen in second. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli has already won the world title, becoming F1’s youngest champion in the process, with three races of the season remaining. The next F1 race is due to be held in Las Vegas on 21 November, before the season concludes in the Middle East with back-to-back races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

The former Manchester City boss came close to taking charge of Italy in the summer and has long been intrigued by working in America, having previously described the USA as "fascinating" for building a long-term project. United States set sights on Guardiola Pochettino is with his United States players ahead of their CONCACAF Nations League fixtures against Haiti this fortnight, but he is expected to join Manchester United once those games are over. United moved closer to appointing the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss after reaching a verbal agreement with him on Wednesday. That would leave the US needing a new head coach, and according to The Athletic , they will make Guardiola their top target. The Spaniard won the Champions League and six Premier League titles at City, having previously enjoyed huge success with Barcelona and Bayern Munich. Guardiola came close to taking Italy job Guardiola has previously shown interest in moving into international football, and he came so close to becoming Italy manager in the summer that he was writing down line-ups before deciding against the role. top.description: The Detroit Lions are bringing back a familiar face just days before their Week 10 showdown against the New England Patriots in Germany. According to the NFL Transactions Log, Detroit has re-signed Jackson Meeks to its practice squad. The move comes just two days after the Lions waived Meeks to make room for veteran safety Andre Cisco, whom Detroit acquired from the New York Jets ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. Now, Meeks is back in the organization, giving Detroit additional offensive depth as the team prepares for the second half of the season. top.title: Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash
top.description: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente said Wednesday he is optimistic Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal will be fit to face England in the Nations League at the weekend. The 19-year-old winger will miss the world champions’ visit to face the Czech Republic in Prague on Thursday with a knee problem and is set to join up with Spain after that game. Yamal played for Barcelona in the 2-1 La Liga win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday and on Monday Spain said he would not travel to face the Czechs. “He got hurt in the last match, he had some discomfort in one knee, he went for the usual treatment, a scan in Barcelona, and they saw he had inflammation and fluid in the knee — that meant he needed rest,” De la Fuente told reporters. “Our medical staff and his medical staff have a fantastic relationship, and I decided that his trip here should be avoided without knowing whether he’d be in any condition to play.” The coach said he had spoken to the winger and his recovery was looking positive ahead of England’s visit to Madrid on Sunday. “He’s doing a series of exercises with his physio and with the club that indicate the recovery is going well,” continued De la Fuente. “We believe, I’m optimistic, that on Friday he’ll be with us.” De la Fuente dismissed the idea that Yamal, who came third in the Ballon d’Or voting in October, has any special privileges compared to his La Roja team-mates. “He has no privileges, and his team-mates are relaxed about it, because we treat everyone the same,” added the coach. “In similar situations we would have done exactly the same for any other player, and the players know that.” – Unstoppable run – Spain have won all four games so far in Group A3 and sealed qualification to the quarter-finals. De la Fuente’s side are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive outings, and the coach said it provided his team with extra motivation. “We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” explained De la Fuente. “None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.” Spain won their previous outing away in Croatia with a brace from Arsenal’s Mikel Merino. The midfielder is frequently used as a substitute by De la Fuente to great effect, with Merino netting vital goals against Portugal and Belgium in the World Cup off the bench this summer. Merino said he would like to be a starter for Spain but he would not kick up a fuss. “Of course, what player wouldn’t like to get (more) minutes?” Merino told reporters. “You’ll never hear me complain about the coach’s decision, I will respect it… but all players want to be important, have minutes and enjoy themselves on the pitch.” The post Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

But yeah, we got a team coming in here on Saturday, and we got to be ready to play.” The No. 10 Cougars (7-2, 4-2) host unranked Baylor 6-3, 4-2) on Saturday, and the sobering thought for Bachmeier and the BYU offense is that the Bears have the No. 18 scoring defense in the country, giving up just 17 points per game. “They are physical and they know their scheme well and they just play ball,” Bachmeier said. Offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick also spoke to reporters Tuesday and said that Bachmeier was one of the reasons why the Cougars gave the Utes their biggest test of the season, throwing for 272 yards and rushing for 59 in BYU’s first loss to Utah since 2019. “He just had a tough day, man. Bear’s been such a good player for us and is still a good player,” Roderick said. “I mean, he made so many good plays in that game that gave us a chance to win, and then just a few bad plays that were costly. But that hasn’t diminished our faith in him one bit.” Monday, offensive lineman Bruce Mitchell said teammates began rallying around Bachmeier and other guys who struggled in front of 52,901 and a national television audience of more than 4 million immediately after the game and continued that throughout the weekend. “I don’t think anybody was too stoked in the locker room following the game, but man, I know Bear, I know the character he has, and I know he’s going to bounce back,” Mitchell said. “It was not just his fault. He’s taking a lot of heat on it, and taking a lot of heat in the media. top.title: Where Will It End? 2nd Tier Schools Want a 2nd CFP Tournament!
top.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images West Virginia athletic director Wren Baker stated that “Yes, there would be a market” for a Group of Six football playoff. This comment came on Wednesday as schools weigh the impact of the upcoming 24-team College Football Playoff . The expansion starts in 2027, and it threatens to push smaller conference teams into a crowded field. Baker’s words signal that schools are already looking for a way to keep their top teams playing for a title. Memphis AD Pushes for Second Chance Memphis athletic director Ed Scott told USA TODAY Sports he has spoken with peers about the idea. “I’ve talked to some other ADs about it,” Scott said during a wide-ranging interview on Wednesday. He does not want Memphis to lose its spot in the big 24-team field, but he sees value in a separate tournament for the rest of the Group of Six. The plan would let a top team from each of the six conferences enter an eight-team bracket. This would happen after the main playoff field is set. It works much as the NIT does for college basketball teams that miss the main NCAA Tournament. Scott noted that the current bowl system is losing its appeal with players. “Bowl games are getting harder to get buy-in from your players, especially after the holidays,” the Memphis AD acknowledged. Players often want to go home for the break, but a championship game offers a better reason to stay. The new playoff would give those teams a real shot at a title rather than a generic bowl matchup. The new playoff could change how the postseason feels for fans in smaller markets. ESPN Paid More to Keep Control The push for expansion came despite strong opposition from the network that holds the rights. Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that the network will pay an additional $345 million per year, on average, for the expanded playoff over the next five years. The deal was finalized on Monday, and it removes the Power 4 conference championship games. ESPN agreed to the terms because the conferences demanded a larger field. The network wanted to keep ownership of the event rather than risk a lowball offer from a competitor. top.title: Pediatric patients cross finish line ahead of Charlotte Marathon
top.description: Ryder crosses the finish line as the 2026 Charlotte Marathon's first "first finisher" at Novant Health Hemby Children's Hospital. About 13,000 runners are expected to hit the streets for the Charlotte Marathon this Saturday, and all of the proceeds benefit Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. While the runners prepare for Saturday’s big and long race, the kids here who will benefit from it were the first finishers to cross the line on Wednesday. Ryder is one of the kids at Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. He’s been cooped up in a room for two days, which is tough for him and his mom. “It’s stressful. And overwhelming. A lot. And then to be confined to 4 walls makes it a little worse. So events like this are really nice,” said Vanessa Villanueva, Ryder’s mom. The Charlotte Marathon is Saturday , and all the proceeds benefit the children’s hospital. One of the child life specialists who helps these kids is also running in the half-marathon Saturday. “It is my first one! Me and a lot of my coworkers are running, so we’re really excited to give back to Novant and help support our patients through that,” said Avery Bradford at Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. “Are you excited or nervous?” asked Channel 9’s Evan Donovan. “Both, for sure both,” Bradford said. For the first time, the marathon is being put on by the Charlotte Sports Foundation, which also puts on the Duke’s Mayo Classic and the Charlotte Invitational. They hope this becomes a community event, not just for runners. “Yes, so that’s something we’re trying to bring forth this year is really capture all the different neighborhoods the runners will be going through and get the community out and cheering. And maybe this can be something the community can own and look forward to every year,” said Kaleah Ellerbe with the Charlotte Sports Foundation. As kids enjoyed blowing bubbles and making signs for the race, Ryder became the first finisher to cross the line. “Ladies and gentlemen, for the 2026 Charlotte Marathon, he’s fast as can be, coming down the chute, he’s our first first-finisher, Ryder,” an announcer said. The Charlotte Marathon is this Saturday morning, and everyone is encouraged to come out and run or cheer. “What I love is it starts in Uptown and then you get to go into Eastover and look at all of the big houses and hear 10,000 footsteps and you get to go through Myers Park, Dilworth, South End, Plaza Midwood, NoDa, all these really unique neighborhoods that make Charlotte special,” said Miller Yoho with the Charlotte Sports Foundation. Channel 9 will have a full wrap-up in our Charlotte Marathon special at noon on Sunday, so if you’re at the race on Saturday, you can still watch.

top.title: UAlbany men's basketball sunk by 3-point barrage in loss to Dartmouth
top.description: UAlbany freshman Tyler Jones drives to the basket in front of Dartmouth sophomore Anton Strelnikov on Wednesday, Nov. 14, 2026, at the Broadview Center in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) ALBANY - The University at Albany men's basketball team knew from its scouting report that Dartmouth wasn't going to be shy about letting the 3-point shots fly in Wednesday's matinee matchup at Broadview Center. When the Big Green started out red-hot from beyond the arc, it put UAlbany in a hole the Great Danes were unable to dig out of - even with a spirited late rally. Dartmouth made its first five 3-point attempts and 7-of-8 overall to start the game, and finished the afternoon 13-of-30 from deep in an 85-76 nonconference win. "They believe so heavily in the 3," UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings said of the Big Green. "So they just keep shooting, and I think they shot themselves into a pretty good game today." Killings lamented the defensive struggles that UAlbany (2-2 overall) had against a Dartmouth (3-1) team that entered Wednesday averaging 32.3 3-point attempts per game, but was shooting just 30.9% from beyond the arc. Against UAlbany, with the Great Danes struggling to cover in man-to-man sets and forced to rely on a 1-3-1 zone, Dartmouth shot 43.3% from deep. "We need to clean up everything defensively," said UAlbany freshman guard Tyler Jones, who finished with 15 points and eight assists. "We have to be dogs on the court. We knew that they shoot 3s," added freshman forward Erwann Bussing, who had his best game in a UAlbany uniform with 11 points. "We can't let them in the first half be 7-of-13. We have to be better than that." Dartmouth's hot shooting start allowed the Big Green to forge a 49-36 halftime lead. The advantage eventually pushed to as many as 18 points with 8:53 left in the second half before UAlbany finally made a run. The Great Danes put a serious scare into the Big Green, with a 10-0 run making it a 78-74 game when Bussing scored with 53 seconds left. But on Dartmouth's ensuing trip down the floor, the Big Green burned nearly the entire 30-second shot clock before Cameron Hiatt drained a corner 3 that iced the win. "We trapped, and they got out. We stayed solid, and then they bury a 3 that killed us," Killings said. "I thought we needed one more stop, and then it's a one-possession game. … They executed better than we did." Dan Civello scored 16 points to lead three Dartmouth players in double figures. Ten different players scored at least four points for the Big Green, and coach Brett MacConnell deployed a substitution pattern that essentially split his team into two five-man units who played together nearly exclusively. Ollie Engen finished with a game-high 18 points and added five assists for UAlbany. Jones' 15-point night was the fourth straight double-figure scoring game for the highly touted freshman , while Bussing and Abdoulaye Fall each scored 11. top.title: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland
top.description: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland Perhaps the most difficult task for the Manchester City hierarchy when constructing Enzo Maresca’s squad is finding quality cover for Erling Haaland. Haaland will play the majority of games up front for City. Given his stature in the game and his goalscoring prowess, Haaland is almost a permanent fixture in City’s starting lineup. Finding a player who will be happy to be used sparingly and as Haaland’s backup is no easy task. There are two routes for City to take to find quality cover for Haaland. They could find a young striker to develop behind Haaland. The alternative is to find an experienced striker who is happy to prove himself at City by playing a vital role for Enzo Maresca’s side. Club Brugge’s impressive young striker Nicolo Tresoldi fits the bill as a young striker that City could target in January. However, a new report has named Bournemouth’s hard-working striker Evanilson as a potential transfer target for Manchester City in January. Evanilson ticks the box of an experienced striker who could provide quality cover for Erling Haaland if City did pursue a move in January. Manchester City have reportedly been tracking the performances of Evanilson in recent weeks. Mark Brus has reported via his exclusive Daily Briefing column that Manchester City, alongside Arsenal, are keeping tabs on the performances of Evanilson for Bournemouth. On City’s interest in Evanilson, Brus reports: “ Manchester City’s technical staff and scouting department have been closely monitoring Evanilson in recent weeks. Internal technical evaluations suggest that he’s seen as someone who could adapt quickly to Enzo Maresca’s system and add significant dynamism to the frontline. ” It is further reported that Arsenal and Manchester City could be prepared to move for Evanilson in January. Brus adds that Bournemouth could slap a €60 million price tag on their Brazilian striker to fend off any interest from clubs. Lastly, it is also reported that Evanilson could be interested in a move away from Bournemouth if the right opportunity arises. In terms of finding a striker who could come in and do a job for City, Evanilson ticks all of the right boxes. Evanilson could be the ideal striker for Manchester City to target. The 27-year-old Brazilian striker is a proven performer. During his time at FC Porto, he scored 60 goals in 154 appearances. After signing for Bournemouth, Evanilson has scored 25 goals and added 14 assists in 86 appearances. Those numbers don’t jump off the page. However, Evanilson is a proven goalscorer although there is more to his game. Evanilson is very good at dropping into space between the midfield and defence to link Bournemouth’s play. He often does this for Marco Rose’s side. Also, Evanilson is often seen drifting wide to become another attacking option for Bournemouth. nigeria.title: Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash
nigeria.description: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente said Wednesday he is optimistic Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal will be fit to face England in the Nations League at the weekend. The 19-year-old winger will miss the world champions’ visit to face the Czech Republic in Prague on Thursday with a knee problem and is set to join up with Spain after that game. Yamal played for Barcelona in the 2-1 La Liga win over Atletico Madrid on Sunday and on Monday Spain said he would not travel to face the Czechs. “He got hurt in the last match, he had some discomfort in one knee, he went for the usual treatment, a scan in Barcelona, and they saw he had inflammation and fluid in the knee — that meant he needed rest,” De la Fuente told reporters. “Our medical staff and his medical staff have a fantastic relationship, and I decided that his trip here should be avoided without knowing whether he’d be in any condition to play.” The coach said he had spoken to the winger and his recovery was looking positive ahead of England’s visit to Madrid on Sunday. “He’s doing a series of exercises with his physio and with the club that indicate the recovery is going well,” continued De la Fuente. “We believe, I’m optimistic, that on Friday he’ll be with us.” De la Fuente dismissed the idea that Yamal, who came third in the Ballon d’Or voting in October, has any special privileges compared to his La Roja team-mates. “He has no privileges, and his team-mates are relaxed about it, because we treat everyone the same,” added the coach. “In similar situations we would have done exactly the same for any other player, and the players know that.” – Unstoppable run – Spain have won all four games so far in Group A3 and sealed qualification to the quarter-finals. De la Fuente’s side are unbeaten in their last 43 competitive outings, and the coach said it provided his team with extra motivation. “We want to keep setting new milestones, and this is another one,” explained De la Fuente. “None of us would probably ever have thought we’d even reach 35, because we already felt those were astronomical numbers, but having reached 43, you think, my goodness, we want to get to 44, of course we do.” Spain won their previous outing away in Croatia with a brace from Arsenal’s Mikel Merino. The midfielder is frequently used as a substitute by De la Fuente to great effect, with Merino netting vital goals against Portugal and Belgium in the World Cup off the bench this summer. Merino said he would like to be a starter for Spain but he would not kick up a fuss. “Of course, what player wouldn’t like to get (more) minutes?” Merino told reporters. “You’ll never hear me complain about the coach’s decision, I will respect it… but all players want to be important, have minutes and enjoy themselves on the pitch.” The post Spain coach optimistic over Yamal’s fitness for England Nations League clash appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.description: The Canada government has announced plans to accelerate permanent residence (PR) processing for up to 200,000 foreign nationals already living in the country in 2027, as part of efforts to reduce immigration application backlogs and provide greater certainty for newcomers. The initiative, announced by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) under the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan, will provide additional admissions spaces for selected workers and humanitarian applicants seeking to transition to permanent residence. According to the government, the measure will be implemented through two major groups: a workers’ cohort and a humanitarian cohort, with up to 100,000 spaces allocated to each. The workers’ category will cover eligible foreign workers already living in Canada, alongside their accompanying family members. The government intends to work with provincial and territorial authorities to identify workers who meet regional labour market requirements. Eligible workers will include those who qualify for permanent residence through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), as well as applicants awaiting decisions under selected federal immigration programmes. These programmes include the Atlantic Immigration Program, Start-Up Visa Program, Self-Employed Persons Program, Agri-Food Pilot and Home Care Worker programmes. The humanitarian category, also allocated up to 100,000 spaces, will cover people already in Canada who have been waiting for permanent residence decisions, including applicants under specific family reunification and humanitarian pathways. Among those expected to benefit from the humanitarian allocation are: Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children: Family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who have already applied for permanent residence and are awaiting final decisions. Hong Kong residents: Applicants under Canada’s permanent residence pathways for Hong Kong residents, which closed to new applications on August 31, 2026. Ukrainian nationals: Applicants under the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway, which closed to new applications on October 22, 2024. Humanitarian and compassionate applicants: Individuals already in Canada whose applications for permanent residence have received approval in principle. The government said the additional spaces would help it process all remaining applications under the Hong Kong and Ukraine pathways, while also supporting family reunification and fulfilling existing humanitarian commitments. IRCC also said the initiative would help reduce waiting periods for spouses and partners of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with the aim of bringing processing times closer to 12 months for applicants destined for provinces outside Quebec. nigeria.title: US withdraws from U17 World Cup in Qatar over security fears
nigeria.description: The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 soccer World Cup in Qatar due to concerns about security in the Middle East, US media reported Wednesday. Players were informed of the decision just over a week before the tournament is due to begin on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported, citing anonymous sources. US Soccer, the sport’s governing body in the United States, did not immediately confirm the news or respond to AFP’s request for comment. The war in the Middle East began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which retaliated by targeting, among others, Gulf countries allied with Washington. Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have been punctuated by repeated threats from the United States and Israel to resume bombardments of Iran. Multiple sporting events in the Middle East have been affected, including the tennis WTA Finals which were scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia — which neighbors Qatar — but are instead now taking place at Indian Wells in the US. This season’s Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the race in Bahrain was called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by the Houthis in Yemen. The US is one of 48 teams scheduled to play in the Under-17 World Cup, in a group with Montenegro, Chile and Algeria. The Under-17 World Cup shifted to an annual event last year, and is being held in Qatar for five consecutive years. Announcing its host decision in 2024, FIFA said the decision to choose a single host nation for multiple editions centered on the ability to make “use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability”. nigeria.title: Five factors vehicle buyers should consider – Understanding the true cost of ownership in Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Theodore opara Buying a vehicle is a major financial decision, but many Nigerian motorists focus almost entirely on the amount required to acquire one. While the purchase price is an important consideration, it does not tell the complete story of what it takes to own and maintain a vehicle over the years. From routine servicing and parts replacement, to insurance, fuel and unexpected repairs, vehicle ownership comes with recurring expenses that can significantly influence its overall value. For individuals, families and businesses, understanding these costs before making a purchase can help prevent financial surprises and support better decisions. The ownership cost equation Two vehicles with similar showroom prices may have significantly different maintenance requirements and operating costs. One may benefit from an established after-sales network, readily available spare parts and predictable servicing expenses. Another may present challenges when replacement components are required or technical support is unavailable. These differences can influence the overall cost of ownership. For instance, a vehicle that requires expensive repairs or spends considerable time in a workshop may eventually cost its owner more than initially anticipated. For businesses operating fleets, the consequences can be even greater. Every day a vehicle remains unavailable could affect deliveries, customer service, employee movement and revenue generation. Consequently, vehicle buyers should consider not only acquisition costs but also the financial implications of keeping their vehicles operational. Five factors buyers should consider A proper assessment of vehicle ownership costs should include five major areas. First is the purchase price and any associated financing charges. Second is routine maintenance, including scheduled servicing, lubricants, filters, tyres and other consumables. Third is warranty protection, particularly its duration, coverage and exclusions. Fourth is the availability and cost of replacement parts, including access to qualified technicians. Fifth is downtime, which may create additional transportation expenses, lost business opportunities and reduced productivity. Although some expenses are difficult to forecast, obtaining reliable information before purchasing can help buyers make more informed comparisons. The importance of after-sales support Automotive distributors increasingly recognise that customers need more than a vehicle at the point of purchase. They also need dependable support throughout the ownership period. Carloha’s CarlohaCare 6-6-7 programme provides an example of this approach, offering a six-year warranty, six years of free servicing and a seven-day repair promise, subject to applicable conditions. Such commitments demonstrate how after-sales benefits can form part of a vehicle’s overall value proposition. nigeria.title: Hezbollah chief calls Trump’s midterm defeat ‘an opportunity’
nigeria.description: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem hailed on Wednesday President Donald Trump’s recent midterm defeat, describing it as “an opportunity” for his Iran-backed Lebanese movement and other opponents of the US in the region. Trump’s Republican Party suffered massive losses in last week’s elections, in which the Democrats seized control of Congress. The president has admitted that the war he launched with Israel against Iran in February was a key factor in the defeat. “Today, we have a good opportunity. Trump was defeated in the elections… an earthquake has occurred in America,” Qassem said in a speech broadcast live to supporters. “The one confronting Iran, Lebanon, Palestine, Yemen… has lost,” he added, arguing that Trump could “no longer continue as is”. “His defeat has ramifications for us that are in a way positive.” He added that Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu “has been broken” after he too suffered a loss in a recent election. Netanyahu’s bloc fell well short of the 61 seats it needed to stay in power in the October 27 vote, and the Israeli president has since tasked his rival Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government. Hezbollah, which once dominated political life in Lebanon, has been weakened by two wars it waged against Israel since 2023. Most recently, the group drew Lebanon into the broader Middle East war in March by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says have killed more than 4,300 people. Israel continues to occupy swathes of southern Lebanon. Lebanon and Israel concluded a framework agreement in June under US auspices, providing for the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces and the disarmament of Hezbollah, but its implementation has stalled. Qassem reiterated on Wednesday that he refused to disarm his group before an Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon. nigeria.title: Uganda ruling party rejects plan for son to succeed president
nigeria.description: The leadership of Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni’s party has rejected his plan to designate his son, known for boasting of kidnapping and torturing rivals, as his successor, five party sources told AFP on Wednesday. The president’s son, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, 52, is currently head of the army, and wields huge and growing influence as his 82-year-old father plays a declining role in governing the east African country after four decades in power. “Muhoozi”, as he is widely known, has vowed to run in the next presidential election scheduled for 2031, but many are unnerved by his flouting of the law, and inflammatory posts on social media, where he frequently boasts of torturing opponents in his “basement”. In recent months, he has had political rivals imprisoned, threatened to behead opposition leader Bobi Wine, and forced the closure of the country’s leading independent media group for several weeks. Although Museveni has ruled with an iron grip since 1986, many within his party, the National Resistance Movement (NRM), have voiced concern at the apparent moves to hand power to his son. In a closed-door meeting of the NRM’s executive committee on Tuesday, convened to determine a successor, a vote on the son’s candidacy had to be abandoned as several of the 28 members spoke against the plan and received loud cheers, according to five people present. Four people had voted in favour of the son, three had voted against, by the time the vote was called off, the sources told AFP. “The combative nature of the (army chief) has created uneasiness among some people. He is fighting and threatening people on social media. Let him start convincing people but not using coercive means to capitulate the population,” said one source. NRM vice-chairman Calvin Echodu told Museveni to retire the son from the army and give him a civilian assignment to get acquainted with the population and prepare himself well for leadership,” said another participant. Echodu also reportedly advised the president that he should stand again in 2031 “as his son is not yet ready,” the source added. The attendees say it was an unprecedented show of defiance against the long-ruling president, who first broached the subject of his succession by presenting a paper to the party grandees in late October, in which he suggested his son had the right credentials for the job. In recent days, Kainerugaba has once again drawn attention with bellicose posts on X, threatening Vice President Jessica Alupo with arrest over claims she was involved in a plot to overthrow the government. The call was made at the 2026 Annual General Meeting (AGM) and Scientific Conference of the Medical Women’s Association of Nigeria (MWAN), Lagos State Branch, where the keynote speaker, Professor Kikelomo Ololade Wright, challenged female doctors to move beyond clinical practice and take their rightful place in healthcare policy formulation and strategic decision-making. Speaking on the theme, “Women Physicians at the Forefront of Health Equity: Advancing Women, Children and Community Health”, Wright said the scale of maternal mortality in Nigeria demanded more decisive action from government, healthcare professionals and other stakeholders. According to her, United Nations figures showed that approximately 75,000 Nigerian women died from pregnancy and childbirth-related complications in 2023, representing nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths recorded globally. “That is one woman every seven minutes,” she said, describing the situation as alarming, particularly because many of the deaths were preventable. Wright, a Professor of Public Health and Community Medicine at the Lagos State University College of Medicine, insisted that women physicians must not limit their contributions to treating patients but should also influence the policies and decisions that determine healthcare delivery. “Not on the sidelines, not behind, not supporting, but we’re at the front,” she declared, stressing that women doctors must be represented in hospital boards, health committees and other decision-making platforms. “We deliver most of the care. We must also shape the decisions. It is non-negotiable,” she added. She said Nigeria’s maternal mortality ratio of estimated 993 deaths per 100,000 live births was about five times the global average and significantly higher than the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of 70 deaths per 100,000 live births. nigeria.title: Beyond The Sole: How Nigerian Artist Eugene Is Turning Waste Into Beauty For A Better World
nigeria.description: An art project that started as a final-year assessment at Auchi Polytechnic, Auchi, Edo State, Nigeria, has turned into a full-time career for Konboye Eugene. In his studio in Kuto, Abeokuta, Ogun State, the Nigerian artist is giving discarded footwear a new lease of life, transforming them into colourful portraits. “I’ve been a full-time studio practitioner for about seven years now. I started when I was in my final year at Auchi Polytechnic, where I studied painting,” Eugene said. “It started as an assignment for me when I was in school. But over the course of my practice, I have become a bit more environmentally aware.” ﻿ Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Materials ‘Everywhere, Anywhere’ Eugene’s craft draws attention to the environmental impact of discarded footwear and the need for better ways to manage waste. “I source my material through landfills, the streets, literally everywhere, anywhere,” he added. This image shows Eugene assessing discarded footwear he used for his artwork. (Photo: ChannelsTV/Kenny Akinwunmi) The artist shares the detailed process of how he brings each work of art to life. “My process entails getting the materials first, after which we wash them. After we wash them, we have to select and separate them according to their colours, tones, and values.” “I work in two different ways. There’s the assemblage part, where I assemble the footwear. And there’s also the tapestry, where I have to break them into tiny circles and fix them together using copper and aluminium wire,” Eugene explained. Statistics cited by Green Network Asia indicate that over 200 million pairs of flip-flops are discarded each year globally, contributing significantly to plastic and rubber pollution in landfills and oceans. Creating each piece of artwork comes with its challenges, as Eugene says the process can take between two and six months, depending on its size and complexity. “There are a whole lot of challenges that come with the work. There are times when we’re working and have creative blockages. And also, because we work with sharp objects like knives, needles, and all that, there’s also the hazard that comes with it. “I think we work between two to six months, depending on the size and complexity of what we’re working on in the studio,” he said. For Eugene, the message goes beyond the finished artwork, as he hopes his work will change how people perceive and handle discarded materials. “These are materials that are known to be non-biodegradable, meaning all the footwear that I’ve used over the course of the years, they’re all out there. entertainment.title: Awar Odhiang Named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026
entertainment.description: Awar Odhiang featured in Vogue wearing a floral printed dress and sculpted oversized rose headpiece. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Remember the model who turned the finale of Matthieu Blazy ‘s first Chanel show into one of the most talked-about runway moments of 2025? That was Awar Odhiang, and she has another major reason to celebrate. The South Sudanese-Canadian model has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026. The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. She is now represented by major modelling agencies across London, Milan, Paris and New York. Awar Odhiang walking the red carpet at the 2026 Met Gala in New York City. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her runway résumé includes shows for Prada, Versace, Miu Miu, Saint Laurent and Jacquemus, but it was her appearance at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2026 show in October 2025 that introduced her to an even wider audience. Closing Matthieu Blazy’s first collection for the fashion house, Awar wore the show’s bridal look, featuring an oversized white shirt and a voluminous, colourful feathered skirt. But it was what happened at the finale that captured everyone’s attention. As the models gathered for their final walk, Awar broke formation, smiling, clapping and twirling in her skirt. When Blazy appeared, she ran towards him and embraced him. The spontaneous moment quickly went viral, with fashion fans celebrating the joy she brought to the runway. entertainment.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
entertainment.description: Two people engaging with technology in a contemporary hotel lobby work setting. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. You can share an idea, ask questions about its strengths and weaknesses, and explore ways to develop it. However, brainstorming should not become an excuse to surrender your imagination. Let AI expand your thinking, not replace it. Use AI to Improve Your Work, Not Replace Your Skills This is becoming more important. AI can help you identify grammatical errors, improve sentence construction, organise information, summarise lengthy documents and make your communication clearer. It can reduce the time spent on repetitive tasks and create more room for important responsibilities. The important thing is that you should remain actively involved. It lists Bastardo No. 15 organizationally, Romero No. 18 and Wehunt No. 19. SoxProspects.com ranks Wehunt No. 13, Bastardo 18th and Romero 22nd. The Sox don’t have any obvious no-doubt-about-it additions. So although Breslow said Boston will operate as if the draft will happen, perhaps the Sox will take their chances and add nobody to the 40-man roster with roster spots limited anways this offseason. That said, Romero, Wehunt and Bastardo are all interesting names to watch at the deadline next Tuesday. Romero might be the most intriguing Rule 5 Draft eligible player of the group because of his background as a first-round draft pick. The Red Sox selected him 24th overall in 2022, he’s still young and injuries have limited his development time in the minors. There’s still plenty of room to improve with more reps. Romero had the second highest hard-hit percentage (41.7%) among Worcester players (minimum 120 plate appearances) behind only Mickey Gasper , who had a 46.5% hard-hit percentage in 238 plate appearances. He also trailed only Gasper in average exit velocity (90.8 mph) and adjusted exit velocity (92.5 mph) for WooSox hitters with 120 or more plate appearances. sports.title: What should the Oregon Ducks expect from Michigan's defense?
sports.description: The Oregon Ducks will host the Michigan Wolverines at Autzen Stadium this weekend for the first time since 2003, but this time it will be the Wolverines looking to play spoiler to the Ducks ' postseason hopes. Michigan has the defense to do it, while the offense remains another story . With NFL talent and plenty of veteran leadership on hand, the moment in front of a raucous Oregon crowd shouldn't be too threatening to the Wolverines, and it could create a low-scoring affair. Oregon is fresh off a 41-28 blowout on the road over Ohio State , while Michigan fell at home to rival Michigan State, 15-6, despite keeping the Spartans out of the end zone. Michigan's defense has been up to the task against everyone on the schedule this season, but Oregon presents the biggest test yet. Conversely, the Ducks have been rolling on offense after making changes to the coaching staff, but the Wolverines might be a difficult matchup. The Ducks don't have any margin for error, but the Wolverines have a stout secondary and an aggressive front seven that could slow Oregon's momentum. Let's take a look at what Michigan does on defense schematically, who to watch out for, and what the Ducks might be able to do to put points on the board. What does Michigan do well on defense? Defensive coordinator Jay Hill operates out of an aggressive 4-2-5 nickel defense that relies on simulated pressures and physical play in the secondary. The Wolverines play more man coverage than the average defense, relying on defensive backs getting their hands on receivers to force them off their lines and tip passes away before an elite wideout has a chance. Michigan has limited opponents to 154.8 passing yards per game, fifth-best in the country. When playing zone coverage, Michigan runs plenty of different pressures while having an experienced front four that can get after the quarterback by itself. The Wolverines play out of the nickel to allow an extra rusher in different looks, and when a team comes out in 12 personnel (one running back, two tight ends), the defense often shifts into a 4-3 look to help stop the run. That balance has helped Michigan rank among the best defenses in the country, limiting opponents to just 16.2 points per game (16th in the nation) and 100.6 rushing yards per game (17th). Players to Know DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley was the biggest transfer portal acquisition in the offseason for Michigan, following Kyle Whittingham from Utah, where he was a first-team All-American last season. Daley has picked up where he left off, leading the Wolverines with six sacks and nine tackles for loss. Michigan has several good pass rushers up front, including Dom Nichols and Tariq Boney, but Daley is by far the biggest threat that the Ducks will need to keep an eye on. He had his best game of the season last week against Michigan State, racking up eight tackles, two sacks and a forced fumble. sports.title: Lewis Hamilton demands Israel allows aid into Gaza after Rafah visit: ‘No excuse’
sports.description: Lewis Hamilton has said Israel must let aid trucks into Gaza in a passionate Instagram post, a day after he toured the Rafah border crossing in Egypt . The seven-time Formula One world champion arrived in El Arish on Tuesday, and during the trip he was briefed on how aid is prepared and coordinated before it is sent into Gaza, as he toured the Rafah crossing and the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses. Following the visit, Hamilton took to Instagram to send a clear message to Israel and his 44.4 million followers. "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling. It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less," the Ferrari driver wrote on Instagram. Israel strongly denies accusations of genocide and says its military campaign in Gaza targets Hamas militants. Hamilton described seeing food trucks lined up and ready to go at the border that were regularly held up or faced major delays. Hamilton poses for a photo with Egyptian Red Crescent members (AFP/Getty) He said that at a nearby logistics centre, items had been rejected for "crazy reasons", including sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, and footballs for children. "Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse," he said. "I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away." Hamilton, 41, is an advocate for humanitarian causes. In 2021 he founded Mission 44, a charity that supports young people and works to improve their access to education and employment. The Brit is currently fourth in the F1 drivers’ standings, but is just a point behind third-placed George Russell, while he is only 18 adrift of Max Verstappen in second. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli has already won the world title, becoming F1’s youngest champion in the process, with three races of the season remaining. The next F1 race is due to be held in Las Vegas on 21 November, before the season concludes in the Middle East with back-to-back races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

This comment came on Wednesday as schools weigh the impact of the upcoming 24-team College Football Playoff . The expansion starts in 2027, and it threatens to push smaller conference teams into a crowded field. Baker’s words signal that schools are already looking for a way to keep their top teams playing for a title. Memphis AD Pushes for Second Chance Memphis athletic director Ed Scott told USA TODAY Sports he has spoken with peers about the idea. “I’ve talked to some other ADs about it,” Scott said during a wide-ranging interview on Wednesday. He does not want Memphis to lose its spot in the big 24-team field, but he sees value in a separate tournament for the rest of the Group of Six. The plan would let a top team from each of the six conferences enter an eight-team bracket. This would happen after the main playoff field is set. It works much as the NIT does for college basketball teams that miss the main NCAA Tournament. Scott noted that the current bowl system is losing its appeal with players. “Bowl games are getting harder to get buy-in from your players, especially after the holidays,” the Memphis AD acknowledged. Players often want to go home for the break, but a championship game offers a better reason to stay. The new playoff would give those teams a real shot at a title rather than a generic bowl matchup. The new playoff could change how the postseason feels for fans in smaller markets. ESPN Paid More to Keep Control The push for expansion came despite strong opposition from the network that holds the rights. Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that the network will pay an additional $345 million per year, on average, for the expanded playoff over the next five years. While the runners prepare for Saturday’s big and long race, the kids here who will benefit from it were the first finishers to cross the line on Wednesday. Ryder is one of the kids at Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. He’s been cooped up in a room for two days, which is tough for him and his mom. “It’s stressful. And overwhelming. A lot. And then to be confined to 4 walls makes it a little worse. So events like this are really nice,” said Vanessa Villanueva, Ryder’s mom. The Charlotte Marathon is Saturday , and all the proceeds benefit the children’s hospital. One of the child life specialists who helps these kids is also running in the half-marathon Saturday. “It is my first one! Me and a lot of my coworkers are running, so we’re really excited to give back to Novant and help support our patients through that,” said Avery Bradford at Novant Health Hemby Children’s Hospital. “Are you excited or nervous?” asked Channel 9’s Evan Donovan. “Both, for sure both,” Bradford said. For the first time, the marathon is being put on by the Charlotte Sports Foundation, which also puts on the Duke’s Mayo Classic and the Charlotte Invitational. They hope this becomes a community event, not just for runners. “Yes, so that’s something we’re trying to bring forth this year is really capture all the different neighborhoods the runners will be going through and get the community out and cheering. sports.title: UAlbany men's basketball sunk by 3-point barrage in loss to Dartmouth
sports.description: UAlbany freshman Tyler Jones drives to the basket in front of Dartmouth sophomore Anton Strelnikov on Wednesday, Nov. 14, 2026, at the Broadview Center in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) ALBANY - The University at Albany men's basketball team knew from its scouting report that Dartmouth wasn't going to be shy about letting the 3-point shots fly in Wednesday's matinee matchup at Broadview Center. When the Big Green started out red-hot from beyond the arc, it put UAlbany in a hole the Great Danes were unable to dig out of - even with a spirited late rally. Dartmouth made its first five 3-point attempts and 7-of-8 overall to start the game, and finished the afternoon 13-of-30 from deep in an 85-76 nonconference win. "They believe so heavily in the 3," UAlbany coach Dwayne Killings said of the Big Green. "So they just keep shooting, and I think they shot themselves into a pretty good game today." Killings lamented the defensive struggles that UAlbany (2-2 overall) had against a Dartmouth (3-1) team that entered Wednesday averaging 32.3 3-point attempts per game, but was shooting just 30.9% from beyond the arc. Against UAlbany, with the Great Danes struggling to cover in man-to-man sets and forced to rely on a 1-3-1 zone, Dartmouth shot 43.3% from deep. "We need to clean up everything defensively," said UAlbany freshman guard Tyler Jones, who finished with 15 points and eight assists. "We have to be dogs on the court. We knew that they shoot 3s," added freshman forward Erwann Bussing, who had his best game in a UAlbany uniform with 11 points. "We can't let them in the first half be 7-of-13. We have to be better than that." Dartmouth's hot shooting start allowed the Big Green to forge a 49-36 halftime lead. The advantage eventually pushed to as many as 18 points with 8:53 left in the second half before UAlbany finally made a run. The Great Danes put a serious scare into the Big Green, with a 10-0 run making it a 78-74 game when Bussing scored with 53 seconds left. But on Dartmouth's ensuing trip down the floor, the Big Green burned nearly the entire 30-second shot clock before Cameron Hiatt drained a corner 3 that iced the win. "We trapped, and they got out. We stayed solid, and then they bury a 3 that killed us," Killings said. "I thought we needed one more stop, and then it's a one-possession game. … They executed better than we did." Dan Civello scored 16 points to lead three Dartmouth players in double figures. Ten different players scored at least four points for the Big Green, and coach Brett MacConnell deployed a substitution pattern that essentially split his team into two five-man units who played together nearly exclusively. Ollie Engen finished with a game-high 18 points and added five assists for UAlbany. Jones' 15-point night was the fourth straight double-figure scoring game for the highly touted freshman , while Bussing and Abdoulaye Fall each scored 11. sports.description: Manchester City may have identified the striker they want to support Erling Haaland Perhaps the most difficult task for the Manchester City hierarchy when constructing Enzo Maresca’s squad is finding quality cover for Erling Haaland. Haaland will play the majority of games up front for City. Given his stature in the game and his goalscoring prowess, Haaland is almost a permanent fixture in City’s starting lineup. Finding a player who will be happy to be used sparingly and as Haaland’s backup is no easy task. There are two routes for City to take to find quality cover for Haaland. They could find a young striker to develop behind Haaland. The alternative is to find an experienced striker who is happy to prove himself at City by playing a vital role for Enzo Maresca’s side. Club Brugge’s impressive young striker Nicolo Tresoldi fits the bill as a young striker that City could target in January. However, a new report has named Bournemouth’s hard-working striker Evanilson as a potential transfer target for Manchester City in January. Evanilson ticks the box of an experienced striker who could provide quality cover for Erling Haaland if City did pursue a move in January. Manchester City have reportedly been tracking the performances of Evanilson in recent weeks. Mark Brus has reported via his exclusive Daily Briefing column that Manchester City, alongside Arsenal, are keeping tabs on the performances of Evanilson for Bournemouth. Brus adds that Bournemouth could slap a €60 million price tag on their Brazilian striker to fend off any interest from clubs. Lastly, it is also reported that Evanilson could be interested in a move away from Bournemouth if the right opportunity arises. In terms of finding a striker who could come in and do a job for City, Evanilson ticks all of the right boxes. Evanilson could be the ideal striker for Manchester City to target. The 27-year-old Brazilian striker is a proven performer. During his time at FC Porto, he scored 60 goals in 154 appearances. After signing for Bournemouth, Evanilson has scored 25 goals and added 14 assists in 86 appearances. Those numbers don’t jump off the page. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted. The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. technology.title: US bit barn boom sees energy needs grow 10x as fast as grid capacity
technology.description: Datacenter power consumption in the US is growing roughly ten times faster than grid capacity, meaning facilities may soon need to find a large chunk of their own electricity from other sources. Surging demand for AI infrastructure is driving a wave of new server farms across America, but it is exposing long-term underinvestment in the grid networks required to deliver power where it's needed. Insurance broker Howden calculates that datacenters would need to source up to 58 percent of their power off the grid by 2030 just to keep their share of grid capacity from growing. Gartner warned in June that the energy consumed by AI datacenters is on track to grow 26 percent this year, and grid supply may be unable to keep pace with demand by the end of this decade. Howden's analysis of data from the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) and S&P Global found that since the year 2000, power being fed to data campuses has risen 19 percent a year on average, while the electricity grid expanded capacity by just 2 percent per annum over the same period. Datacenters' share of US grid capacity was circa five percent in 2025, up from 0.1 percent in 2000 – a 50-fold increase. Management consultancy Bain & Company issued a report two years ago warning that energy companies must switch gear and invest in building out grid capacity faster , as energy draw by server farms is expected to more than double by 2030. This doesn't mean that datacenters are in danger of eating all of America's electricity, at least not in the immediate future. The graph makes it appear that the two lines are about to cross, but the chart uses different scales: 1,400 gigawatts on the left axis for grid capacity, versus just 80 on the right for datacenters. Keeping datacenters at five percent of grid capacity requires 110 gigawatts of behind-the-meter capacity by 2030, Howden estimates – an expansion it considers unlikely. Instead, it expects a combination of greater reliance on the grid, slower development at power-constrained sites, and alternative supplies. For the largest, most power-constrained projects, Howden warns that grid delays of two to six years could mean $800 million to $2.4 billion in forgone revenue. "Power availability is becoming one of the defining challenges of the datacenter boom," says Howden head of Natural Resources Stuart Adam. "As demand for AI infrastructure accelerates, developers are increasingly looking beyond traditional grid connections to secure the electricity they need." Howden's business is insurance, and so Adam also notes that on-site generation introduces new operational and financial exposures, as operators take greater responsibility for their power infrastructure. ®

technology.title: Scientists check their work and confirm it with update on iconic black hole image
technology.description: The image of the red ring around the black hole M87, produced by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) array, made front-page news around the world in 2019. There was one problem: there was a slim chance the depiction might be wrong. This week, a small team of four Australian researchers have published their work confirming the result based on a new machine learning algorithm using the same base data. The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image came from hundreds of scientists working together to capture the first direct view of a black hole's shadow. The measurements were taken at eight telescopes around the world, at locations including Chile, the US, and Antarctica. Reconstructing the image from the data so geographically distant meant instrument and environment errors could influence the accuracy of the resulting image. Potentially, alternative analyses of the data could have reconstructed an image without the iconic ring shape. Samuel Lai – a postdoctoral fellow at the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) in Western Australia – and his team created an independent imaging algorithm to process the historic dataset to validate the result. The new approach used closed triplets (using three telescopes for error correction) rather than station pairs in an effort to reduce error. To the relief of the EHT team, the new image recreated the iconic ring-like image seen in the original, according to a paper published in Nature today . In a prepared statement, Lai said taking pictures of black holes was not easy. "It is like standing in your backyard and trying to take a photo of a doughnut on the Moon," he said. He explained that when his team applied new advanced machine learning and artificial intelligence techniques to the original Event Horizon Telescope dataset, they found a black hole almost identical in size and shape to the historic EHT image. "Importantly, our model had no idea what a black hole looked like when we applied it to the M87 data. This is the first truly independent validation of the EHT image, an important step in the scientific process," he said. Event Horizon Telescope director Laurent Loinard welcomed the new study. "It is extremely gratifying to see that an elegant, entirely independent method recovers the ring structure of M87 across several years, in excellent agreement with the EHT Collaboration's published results," he said. ®

science.title: NASA kick-starts a fresh push to bring Mars samples home
science.description: null A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet. NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for its troubled Mars Sample Return (MSR) program, called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture, or PSRA in space shorthand. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth. The PSRA initiative was noted on Nov. 9 by Tiffany Morgan, director of the NASA Mars Exploration Program (MEP), during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG). Here's the PSRA strategy: Develop impartial recommendations for retrieving the Martian samples collected by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover and deliver them to Earth Assess proposed mission requirements Review prior lessons learned Evaluate current capabilities and acquisition options Morgan noted that there will be a PSRA strategy team kickoff in January 2027 with a final report due in winter 2027-2028. Pick-me-ups The backdrop to the PSRA activity is that there's one busy rover already on the Red Planet snagging and bagging samples. NASA's Perseverance Mars rover remains on the prowl within Jezero Crater following its touchdown in February 2021. That car-sized robot has been grabbing select specimens from across the area and gingerly dropping the sealed pick-me-ups on the surface of Mars , as well as stuffing them inside the rover itself. Those collectibles may well hold signs of past life on the enigmatic, dusty and foreboding Red Planet. NASA and the European Space Agency have for years been intently plotting out plans to send future spacecraft to Mars and haul those Perseverance-plucked bits, pieces, and sniffs of atmosphere to Earth for rigorous inspection here on Earth using state-of-the-art equipment. This photomontage shows each of the sample tubes deposited by NASA's Perseverance Mars rover at the Three Forks sample depot, as viewed by the WATSON camera on the end of the rover's robotic arm. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) Sticker shock However, over the years, multiple reviews of a NASA Mars Sample Return (MSR) project by independent groups have reported sticker shock findings. Indeed, one last price tag came in at about $11 billion, with samples being returned to Earth in 2040. That finding was deemed by NASA itself as too costly and not doable within an acceptable time frame. Yet another appraisal group ended up finding it feasible to return Mars samples as early as 2035 for a less costly ship and shoot cost of some $8 billion. How the PSRA review deals with MSR cost and a multitude of other concerns is in the to-be-determined column. Why samples now? In the first place, why are samples from Mars delivered by robotic means? science.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
science.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space. Catching one takes luck, as a telescope has to be pointed at the right patch of sky at the right moment. That changed with CHIME (the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment) in British Columbia. With a very wide field of view and a supercomputer to process its data, CHIME more than quadrupled the number of known FRBs in its first year of operation alone. Between 2018 and 2023, CHIME recorded 4,539 bursts from 3,641 sources. As pulses of radio waves, our eyes haven't evolved to see FRBs, nor can we hear them as they aren't sound waves. Well, not until now. "Artist and composer Andrew Melchior turned all of the CHIME bursts into sound for "The Logos," an installation that has played daily at Oulu Cathedral in Finland since early April and is scheduled to run through the end of the year. Melchior and Kiyoshi Masui, an associate professor of physics at MIT, "sonified" the bursts, translating data into acoustics so that human ears can hear them. The structure of each real signal is mapped to varying musical pitches and played through 12 loudspeakers spread throughout the cathedral. The result is a range of tones, with distant FRBs humming, rumbling, popping, and whistling. The signals are old by any human measure. According to a description on Melchior's website , the youngest in the work are about 50 million years old, and the oldest are about 8 to 9 billion years old. An animation shows the random appearance of fast radio bursts (FRBs) across the sky (Image credit: NRAO Outreach/T. Jarrett (IPAC/Caltech); B. Saxton, NRAO/AUI/NSF)) Physics also plays a role in what is heard. Each burst arrives with its high frequencies first and sweeps downward, stretched by its journey through intergalactic gas, "and you can hear that dispersion as it falls from the dome," Melchior told Space.com by email.
